name: Perform scheduled turbine service
summary: Every wind turbine gets a semi-annual and an annual service: technicians check bolt torques, change filters, grease bearings, take oil samples, inspect blades, brakes and electrical parts, and test the safety systems. The ERP releases a preventive work order for each service, the site manager places it in the service season plan, and either an own technician pair or, for turbines under a manufacturer service agreement, the manufacturer's crew does the work. Most service is pushed into the low-wind summer months to lose less energy, which crowds the technicians' calendar, and windy days, missing kit and defects found during inspection stretch the schedule.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta-centred listed generator that services most of its southern Alberta wind turbines with its own technicians and buys service for its newest farm from the turbine manufacturer.
baseline.notes: Wind division of about 70 people running roughly 450 turbines on 11 to 12 southern Alberta wind farms commissioned between 1997 and 2021, most of them older 0.66 to 3 MW machines without tower elevators.

trigger: The ERP maintenance plan releases a preventive work order for a turbine's semi-annual or annual service.
end_state: The service checklist is complete, readings and defects are recorded, the turbine is back in remote control and the preventive work order is closed; for manufacturer-performed services the service report is accepted and the ticket approved.

volume.seasonality: Concentrated from May to September, when wind and lost revenue are lowest; little service in December to February.

evidence.note: About 450 turbines with two services a year give about 900 services a year (75 a month on average); scheduled service two to three times a year in pe2008. Turbine count is the organisation file's estimate from the facility list in aif2021.
Wind farms are serviced when wind is low (source); the season length and multiplier are the organisation file's estimates.

roles.title: Wind turbine technician
roles.department: Wind and storage: southern Alberta wind sites

evidence.note: Organisation file role (38 people; days with weekend on-call). Alberta wind technician wages about 32 to 45 CAD/h in 2021 per the organisation file. Loaded = wage x 1.40 (benefits about 25 percent, overhead about 15 percent), as in the organisation file. Steps record the lead technician's minutes; services are done by a pair, so the stated FTE counts both people (about twice the lead's hands-on time).

resources.name: Two-person wind technician team with service truck

steps.name: Release the preventive work order
steps.description: The ERP maintenance plan for the turbine reaches its due date (six or twelve months since the last service) and releases a preventive work order with the task list for a semi-annual or annual service.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Place the service in the season plan
steps.description: In the monthly planning session the site manager slots the released work orders into the service season plan by farm, grouping turbines on the same road, avoiding high-wind months and balancing against expected corrective work.

error.defect_description: Service slotted into a week when the pair is already committed elsewhere.

next.condition: turbine under a manufacturer service agreement

evidence.note: Services are planned for low-wind periods (source); the share serviced by the manufacturer (the newest farm, about 20 percent of services) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Call off the service from the manufacturer
steps.description: For turbines under a manufacturer service agreement the site manager sends the service order to the manufacturer's site lead with the turbines, the window and site access rules, and agrees the dates.

evidence.note: Organisation file notes service agreements with manufacturers; call-off practice estimated.

steps.name: Manufacturer crew services the turbine
steps.description: The manufacturer's crew arrives in its own window, completes its own permits and checklists, services the turbine and sends a service report; the waiting time includes their day or two of work.

error.defect_description: Checklist item skipped or reading missing in the manufacturer report.

evidence.note: Manufacturer crew timing estimated; their working time is folded into the wait because it is not this organisation's labour.

steps.name: Assign the pair and the day
steps.description: The site supervisor assigns the service to a technician pair and a day on the weekly plan, checking that the pair holds the training for the turbine model and that the needed kit is in stock.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Pick the service kit
steps.description: The pair collects the service kit from the site store (oil and air filters, grease cartridges, gear oil, oil sample bottles, consumables), books it to the work order and loads the torque tools on the truck.

error.defect_description: A filter or the right grease is missing from the kit.

evidence.note: Pairs are often pulled onto breakdowns, so planned services slip by days. Estimate.

steps.name: Check the wind forecast for the day
steps.description: Before leaving, the lead technician checks forecast wind speed against the climbing and hoisting limits, because a service needs a full day of hoisting kit and working in the hub.

control.basis: Company climbing and hoisting limits from manufacturer manuals: no nacelle access above about 20 m/s, no hoisting above about 10 m/s, hub entry only at low wind with the rotor locked

next.condition: too windy for hoisting or hub work

evidence.note: Limits from the source; share of lost days estimated even in the summer season.

steps.name: Wait for a low-wind day
steps.description: The service is moved to the next forecast low-wind day and the pair takes other work; in a windy week several services slip together.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive to the turbine
steps.description: The pair drives the loaded service truck from the site office to the turbine over public roads and gravel access roads on leased farmland, opening gates as the landowner agreement requires.

evidence.note: Farms spread around Pincher Creek, Cowley and Fort Macleod (aif2021); drive time estimated.

steps.name: Hazard assessment, lockout and notify the operations centre
steps.description: The pair completes the field-level hazard assessment, calls the operations centre to take the turbine out of service, applies locks and tags and records the permit.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 (hazard assessment) and Part 15 (energy isolation); company permit-to-work standard

evidence.note: Work inside turbines only under a written order or permit (source); durations estimated.

steps.name: Climb and hoist the kit
steps.description: The technicians climb the tower with fall arrest and lift filters, oil drums and torque tools to the nacelle with the service hoist.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 9 (fall protection) and the two-climber rule; hoist used only below the wind limit

evidence.note: Teams of two and hoist limits (ii2025); towers without elevators (pe2008).

steps.name: Check bolt torques
steps.description: Following the task list, the pair torques a sample or all of the blade root, hub, main frame, yaw and tower flange bolts with hydraulic tools, marking checked bolts and noting any found loose; annual services cover more bolts than semi-annual ones.

error.defect_description: Bolts skipped or torqued to the wrong value.

evidence.note: Service downtime of 12 to 18 hours per outage (pe2008) bounds the total; split between tasks estimated.

steps.name: Lubricate, change filters and sample oil
steps.description: The pair greases the main, pitch and yaw bearings, changes gearbox and hydraulic filters, tops up oils and takes a gearbox oil sample for laboratory analysis.

error.defect_description: Oil sample mislabelled or bearing missed.

evidence.note: Within the 12 to 18 hour service downtime in pe2008; split estimated.

steps.name: Inspect components
steps.description: The technicians inspect the blades from the hub and nacelle, the brakes, yaw drives, pitch system, generator, cables, converter cabinet and safety equipment against the checklist, and decide whether any defect needs follow-up work.

next.condition: defect found that needs separate work

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate. Defect share estimated.

steps.name: Test the safety systems
steps.description: The pair tests the emergency stops, safety chain, overspeed protection and brake function, and records the results on the checklist.

control.basis: Manufacturer maintenance manual and the company maintenance standard: safety-chain and emergency-stop tests at every scheduled service

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Descend, remove lockout and return the turbine
steps.description: The pair lowers waste oil and old filters with the hoist, climbs down, removes locks and tags, closes the permit and calls the operations centre to restart the turbine.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 (energy isolation): locks removed only by the workers who applied them

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive back
steps.description: The pair drives back to the site office with waste oil, used filters and samples, and returns unused kit to the store.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter readings and the checklist in the ERP
steps.description: The lead technician types the checklist results, torque and temperature readings, consumables used and hours into the ERP work order and books hours in timekeeping.

error.defect_description: Readings missing or checklist ticked without values.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Ship the oil sample to the laboratory
steps.description: The technician fills in the laboratory form with turbine and gearbox details and ships the oil sample by courier; results arrive weeks later and go to the reliability engineers.

error.defect_description: Sample form incomplete, so the result cannot be matched to the gearbox.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and close the preventive work order
steps.description: In the weekly review the site supervisor checks the completed checklist and readings, approves the hours and closes the preventive work order so the next due date is calculated, or returns it for missing readings.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Raise a corrective notification for the defect
steps.description: For a defect that cannot be fixed during the service (a blade crack, worn yaw brake pads, a leaking pitch cylinder) the technician raises a corrective notification in the ERP with photos so it is planned as a repair.

error.defect_description: Defect described too vaguely to plan the repair.

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the manufacturer service report
steps.description: The site supervisor reads the manufacturer's service report, compares it with the task list, checks readings and open findings, and spot-checks a sample of turbines in the field.

next.condition: punch list items sent back to the manufacturer

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the service ticket
steps.description: The site manager signs the manufacturer's service ticket so it can be matched to the agreement and invoiced, and closes the preventive work order in the ERP.

control.basis: Delegation of authority and service agreement terms: site manager sign-off before an OEM service is invoiced

evidence.note: Common practice for scheduled service of onshore wind turbines in 2019-2022; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Windy day
exceptions.description: Forecast wind is above the hoisting or hub limits and the service slips to the next low-wind day.

exceptions.name: Defect found during inspection
exceptions.description: The inspection finds a defect that needs separate corrective work; a notification is raised and the service continues.

exceptions.name: Manufacturer punch list
exceptions.description: The supervisor finds missing items in the manufacturer report and the crew must return.

benchmarks.unit: hours of turbine downtime per scheduled service

evidence.note: Stated in the source, with two to three scheduled services a year.

benchmarks.unit: average technician presence per preventive maintenance event
benchmarks.population: Onshore and offshore field data, Walgern et al. 2026

evidence.note: Stated in the source; includes shorter inspection visits, so it is below a full annual service.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from work order release to close

evidence.note: Preventive work orders are typically released two to four weeks ahead of the due date and closed in a weekly review; not measured.

pain_points.description: Squeezing most services into the low-wind summer months doubles the workload exactly when breakdowns also need the same technicians.

evidence.note: Service timed to low-wind periods (source); the clash with corrective work is the author's judgement.

pain_points.description: A service ties up a pair for a full day on one turbine, and windy days cancel hoisting and hub work.

evidence.note: 12 to 18 hours downtime per service (pe2008); hoist limit below 10 m/s (ii2025).

pain_points.description: Paper checklists are re-typed into the ERP and readings go missing, weakening the trend data for reliability analysis.

evidence.note: Author's judgement.

sources.title: Keeping Wind Turbines Spinning (S. Blankinship)
sources.supports: Scheduled wind turbine maintenance is usually done two to three times a year with 12 to 18 hours of downtime per outage; wind farms are often serviced when wind is low; replacement components are expensive and time-consuming to replace; older towers without elevators are climbed.

sources.title: Reliability and O&M key performance indicators of onshore and offshore wind turbines based on field-data analysis (Walgern et al.)
sources.supports: Onshore failure rate 3.3 non-resettable failures per turbine per year (1.729 per MW per year); WMEP onshore 2.4 failures per turbine per year for smaller turbines; average technician time on site 2.7 h for component replacements, about 1.5 h for other corrective maintenance and 3.8 h for preventive maintenance, excluding travel and spare-part lead times; pitch, control and converter systems have the highest onshore failure rates per MW.

sources.title: Working as a wind turbine technician: how to minimise risks
sources.supports: Wind speed limits set by regulations and manufacturers: access to the lower platform up to 25 m/s and to the nacelle up to 20 m/s, hoists below 10 m/s; all work by teams of at least two people; work inside turbines only under a written order or permit; work stops and the team evacuates if gusts threaten stability.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Alberta wind facility list with capacities and commissioning years: Castle River (1997-2001), Cowley North and Sinnott (2001, five Nordex N60 1.3 MW turbines), McBride Lake (2004, 50 percent), Summerview 1 (2004) and 2, Blue Trail (2009) and Macleod Flats, Soderglen (2006, 50 percent), Oldman (2007), Ardenville (2010), Windrise (206 MW, commercial operation November 2021); wind speeds are historically greater in the cold winter months.

assumptions: The organisation file lists no trigger for this process. The ERP maintenance plan built from the reliability group's maintenance strategy releases each work order, so triggered_by uses maintenance_strategy from eng-reliability-analysis.
touch_min records the lead technician's minutes; services are done by a pair, so the wind_technician FTE (13) is about twice the lead's hands-on time at 80 percent own-performed services.
About 20 percent of services (the newest farm) are done by the manufacturer's crew under a service agreement; their working time is folded into the wait at s04.
Annual and semi-annual services are averaged in one set of step times; annual services sit toward the high end of the torque and inspection ranges.
Defects found are sent on as work requests to the troubleshoot process; the organisation file does not list this link.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.40).
Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24: technicians climb in pairs, so the steps from the drive to the turbine to the drive back now carry people 2, and the staffing check counts both technicians.
